checks.title: Phone number listed
checks.rubric: A profile without a phone number loses calls from the Maps panel, the most common action local searchers take.
checks.fix: Add the main local phone number in the profile's contact section; use a local number, not a call centre.

checks.title: Website linked
checks.rubric: Without a website link the profile cannot send visitors on, and Google has no site to confirm the business against.
checks.fix: Link the website page for this location (a location page for multi-location brands, otherwise the home page).

checks.title: Opening hours listed
checks.rubric: Missing hours make Google show no open/closed state and push searchers who filter by 'Open now' elsewhere.
checks.fix: Add regular opening hours for every day, and special hours for holidays.

checks.title: Profile claimed
checks.rubric: An unclaimed profile can be edited by anyone and the owner cannot reply to reviews or post updates.
checks.fix: Claim and verify the profile with 'Own this business?' in Maps, from an account the business controls.

checks.title: Not permanently closed
checks.rubric: A profile marked permanently closed drops out of local results.
checks.fix: If the business still trades here, reopen the profile; if it moved, update the address instead of closing.

checks.title: Address or service area shown
checks.rubric: Google needs an address or a service area to know where the business competes.
checks.fix: Add the street address for a storefront, or the service areas for a business that visits customers.

checks.title: Primary category set
checks.rubric: The primary category is the strongest relevance signal a profile has; without one the profile ranks for little.
checks.fix: Pick the most specific primary category that describes the core business, as the top competitors do.

checks.title: Secondary categories used
checks.rubric: Secondary categories let the profile rank for the other services it sells; Google allows up to nine.
checks.fix: Add the secondary categories that match services actually offered; never add ones that do not apply.

checks.title: Primary category fits the target search
checks.rubric: When the primary category does not share words with the search the business wants, it rarely ranks for it.
checks.fix: Choose a primary category that matches the main search; move the current one to a secondary slot if it still applies.

checks.title: Uses the categories top competitors share
checks.rubric: A category most of the top competitors use and this profile lacks is a likely relevance gap.
checks.fix: Review the categories competitors share and add those that describe this business truthfully.

checks.title: Description written
checks.rubric: The description is the one place the owner explains the business in their own words.
checks.fix: Write a description of what the business does, for whom and where, with no links or promotions.

checks.title: Description length
checks.rubric: Google allows 750 characters; under about 250 says too little to show relevance.
checks.fix: Expand the description to between 250 and 750 characters, leading with the core services.

checks.title: Description names the service and the place
checks.rubric: A description that names the main service and the city confirms relevance for local searches.
checks.fix: Mention the main service and the city or area served in the first sentence of the description.

checks.title: Attributes filled
checks.rubric: Attributes (accessibility, payments, amenities) feed filters and answers; few means missed matches.
checks.fix: Fill every attribute that applies in the profile's 'More' section.

checks.title: Services listed
checks.rubric: Listed services help the profile match service searches and appear in the profile's services tab.
checks.fix: List each service sold, with a short description, using the words customers search with.

checks.title: Products listed
checks.rubric: Products show as a carousel on the profile; they are optional for service-only businesses.
checks.fix: Add the main products or service packages with a photo, a name and a price range.

checks.title: Enough photos
checks.rubric: Profiles with few photos look abandoned and get fewer clicks and direction requests.
checks.fix: Add real photos of the exterior, interior, team and work; keep adding a few each month.

checks.title: Customers add photos to reviews
checks.rubric: Reviews with photos are more trusted; almost none suggests customers are not asked for them.
checks.fix: When asking for reviews, invite customers to add a photo of the result.

checks.title: Rating
checks.rubric: Searchers filter and choose by stars; under 4.0 loses clicks to better-rated neighbours.
checks.fix: Fix the causes the negative reviews name, then ask every satisfied customer for a review.

checks.title: Enough reviews
checks.rubric: A handful of reviews is weak proof for searchers and a weak prominence signal for Google.
checks.fix: Ask for a review after each completed job, with a direct review link.

checks.title: Review count against competitors
checks.rubric: Far fewer reviews than the competitors' median is one of the clearest prominence gaps in local results.
checks.fix: Set a monthly review target that closes the gap to the competitors' median within a year.

checks.title: Recent reviews
checks.rubric: Review velocity matters: no new reviews in three months reads as a business in decline.
checks.fix: Make asking for a review part of every job, so new reviews arrive every month.

checks.title: Owner replies to reviews
checks.rubric: Replying to reviews shows searchers the owner cares, and Google says it is a good practice.
checks.fix: Reply to every review, positive and negative, ideally within a few days.

checks.title: Owner replies quickly
checks.rubric: A reply weeks later helps little; a quick reply can turn an unhappy reviewer around.
checks.fix: Check new reviews weekly and reply within a few days.

checks.title: No unanswered negative reviews
checks.rubric: A recent one- or two-star review with no reply is the first thing a careful searcher reads.
checks.fix: Reply to each negative review calmly and specifically, and offer to resolve it offline.

checks.title: Posted recently
checks.rubric: Posts older than a month show an inactive profile; regular posts keep offers and news in front of searchers.
checks.fix: Publish an update, offer or event post at least weekly.

checks.title: Posting cadence
checks.rubric: A steady rhythm of posts beats bursts followed by silence.
checks.fix: Plan a month of posts ahead and publish on a fixed day each week.

checks.title: Posts link somewhere
checks.rubric: A post without a call-to-action button gives the reader nothing to do next.
checks.fix: Add a button (Book, Order, Learn more, Call) that links to the matching page.

checks.title: Posts carry a photo or video
checks.rubric: Text-only posts are easy to scroll past.
checks.fix: Attach a real photo or short video to every post.

checks.title: Website matches name, address and phone
checks.rubric: A website that shows a different name, address or phone weakens Google's trust in the profile's details.
checks.fix: Show the exact profile name, address and phone on the linked page, in text and in schema.

checks.title: LocalBusiness schema present
checks.rubric: LocalBusiness structured data states the business's details in a form search engines and agents read reliably.
checks.fix: Add LocalBusiness JSON-LD (or the most specific subtype) to the linked page.

checks.title: LocalBusiness schema complete
checks.rubric: Schema without address, telephone, geo or opening hours leaves out the facts local search needs.
checks.fix: Add name, address, telephone, geo and openingHoursSpecification to the LocalBusiness schema.

checks.title: Click-to-call link
checks.rubric: Mobile visitors expect to tap the number; a number that is only text costs calls.
checks.fix: Wrap the phone number in a tel: link.

checks.title: Website hours match the profile
checks.rubric: Different hours on the website and the profile confuse customers and Google.
checks.fix: Make the hours on the website and its schema the same as the profile's.

checks.title: Embedded map
checks.rubric: An embedded Google map on the location page helps visitors find the business and ties the page to the place.
checks.fix: Embed the Google map of this business on the contact or location page.

checks.title: Name free of keyword stuffing
checks.rubric: Adding cities or services to the business name breaks Google's guidelines and risks suspension; competitors can report it.
checks.fix: Use the real-world business name as on signage and documents; put services and places in categories and the description.

checks.title: Service-area business hides its street address
checks.rubric: A business that serves customers at their location but shows a street address where it does not receive them risks suspension.
checks.fix: If customers are not served at the address, hide it and keep only the service areas.

checks.title: Not temporarily closed
checks.rubric: A profile marked temporarily closed ranks lower and tells searchers to go elsewhere.
checks.fix: Remove the temporary closure as soon as the business reopens.

checks.title: No duplicate-looking profiles at the same address
checks.rubric: Two profiles with similar names at one address look like duplicates; Google may merge or suspend them.
checks.fix: Check each same-address profile; request removal of true duplicates through Google support.
